items.title: BIO26 Healthcare Special Address
items.summary:
NVIDIA released a new toolkit called BioNeMo Agent Toolkit that's meant to let AI agents actually do hands-on scientific work in biology and chemistry - not just answer questions about it. Instead of an AI just chatting about a protein or a drug compound, it can now use real scientific software tools: predicting protein shapes, testing how well a drug molecule binds to a target, analyzing genetic sequencing data, and suggesting which lab experiments to try next.

Companies including Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Eli Lilly, Schrödinger, Snowflake, and the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design are adopting it, and both Anthropic and OpenAI are integrating it into their systems. The idea is that a general AI chatbot is bad at knowing which specialized scientific tool to use for a given task - this toolkit hands it the right tools and know-how so it can work more like a research assistant.

items.summary:
BioNeMo Agent Toolkit is an open, agent-ready toolkit that gives any AI agent callable tools for protein structure prediction, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomic analysis, and more. Built on more than a decade of NVIDIA life sciences libraries and models, BioNeMo Agent Toolkit has tools and skills for agentic software throughout the full drug discovery stack: from early biology to molecular design to translational science.

items.title: Enhancements to Time Series and Tabular Frameworks and New Model Fitting in V15
items.summary:
Since Version 10 (in 2014), Wolfram Language has featured a time series construct for representing data through time. In Version 15, we have a much stronger and fully compatible version of TimeSeries, capable of handling larger and more varied datasets. Our new TimeSeries framework is based on the Tabular framework that we introduced in Version 14.2 and interoperates with it. In Version 15, we're also introducing a powerful new, unified approach to data fitting and inference. The new function ModelFit supports quantities and dates natively and works with both machine learning and statistical models.
Check out all the webinars in this series for a deep dive into select areas of Wolfram Language and Mathematica 15: https://www.bigmarker.com/series/new-in-wolfram-language-15/series_details
